newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM CEO sees pulp signalling turnaround.
newsitem.headline: UPM CEO sees pulp signalling turnaround.

text.p: Juha Niemela, CEO of Europe's biggest forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy, said on Thursday that the rise in pulp prices was signalling a turnaround for the whole sector.
"Judging by past performance, a rise in pulp prices means a turnaround for the forest industry," Niemela told a news conference.
He said there was "strong faith" in the markets that recently announced long-fibre pulp price hikes to $580 per tonne from $520 per tonne would come true.
"I would expect $580 to become the sales price sometime in the summer, at the latest by early autumn," Niemela said, adding that $580 was already the market price in the United States.
Earlier, UPM-Kymmene said in a statement with its first quarter results that it expected sales prices for printing and writing papers to rise marginally during the first half of the year.
The already announced five to eight percent increase in light-weight coated paper (LWC) prices was likely to materialise in the second quarter, or by July, Niemela said.
On newsprint, UPM-Kymmene said European prices were expected to benefit later this year from a rise in consumption and prices which had started in North America.

Niemela saw scope for increased European paper consumption in 1997, mainly due to an expected increase in European growth, and since paper stocks held by customers and distributors were estimated to be about normal.
